title: ai-payback: an open instrument for assessing whether enterprise AI adoption pays back
description:
An open-source instrument that produces the ROI analysis document AI adoption maturity frameworks require organisations to hold but do not define how to produce.

Scores 78 diagnostic questions across 26 barriers in three layers (algorithms; technology and data; people and processes) weighted 10/20/70; builds a total cost of ownership across categories routinely omitted from AI budgets; and computes simple payback, or refuses to and says why.

Design commitments enforced as tests: an unanswered question is never scored as zero; an unpriced cost is never treated as zero; no number is invented; payback is refused rather than fabricated; every coefficient carries a provenance tier and a verification date; and a benefit supplied without a named conversion path is reported with an explicit caveat, because at national scale 95.7% of AI-using firms record no AI-driven employment change at all.

Not affiliated with NIST, CMU SEI, Accenture, MIT Project NANDA or BCG. Every mapping to their published work is this project's own reading of public documents.
notes: The framework operationalises Yedigeyeva, M. K. (2026), 'Problems of implementing artificial intelligence in enterprises. Reasons for low return on investment and management solutions', Ekonomika i upravlenie: problemy, resheniya 11(5), pp. 263-280. Implementation was AI-assisted; this is recorded in the repository's commit history.
